subject: ACME renewal & expansion - recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sabrina Li <sabrina.li@acme.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: ACME renewal & expansion - recap and next steps

Hi Sabrina / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please reply with any corrections.

What we reviewed
- Current usage: ~1.2B tokens/month (chat + batch inference), with a spike pattern around marketing sends and nightly batch ranking jobs.
- Pain points: latency spikes on peak chat routing (~600-800ms p95), embedding costs for search/semantic ranking, and insufficient visibility into per-route token costs.
- Goals for next 12 months: reduce per-token inference cost by ~30% for batch workloads, bring p95 chat latency under 300ms, and onboard embeddings for product search (pilot: 5M rows).

Recommended upsell path
1) Pilot Dedicated pool for high-throughput batch (3x reserved GPUs) to reduce unit costs + prefix cache.
2) Dedicated instance for production chat traffic with latency SLOs and canary rollout.
3) Redwood Optimize eval and recommendations (quantization + batching) during pilot to hit the 30% cost target.

Timeline
- Procurement kickoff: early March (finance review + pricing breakdown)
- Pilot launch: mid-March (2–4 weeks)
- Renewal / expansion effective date: target April 1, 2026

Attachments: ACME_usage_report_Q4_2025.pdf (usage + spike analysis), Redwood_pricing_proposal_v2.pdf (detailed pricing and seat/commit options).

Action items / next steps
- Marissa: Share pricing breakdown and proposal (attached).
- ACME: Confirm procurement contact and preferred week for follow-up demo (week of Mar 1st suggested).
- Michael & Vivek: Prepare pilot plan (canary criteria, telemetry to monitor).

Thanks — I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up for the week of Mar 1 unless you suggest otherwise.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0183

Thanks Marissa — nice summary. Couple quick notes from our side:
- Confirmed pain points — latency during peak chat hours is the biggest blocker for product adoption this quarter.
- Finance will need a line-item breakdown (embedded vs. inference tokens vs. dedicated capacity) and a clear cost comparison to our current infra. Could you provide that by end of next week?
- We’re supportive of a mid-March pilot; prefer a hard demo on Tue, Mar 3 or Wed, Mar 4.

I’ll get Sabrina (procurement) and our finance lead looped if we move forward.

Tom

Marissa / Vivek —

Adding a few internal notes to shape the pilot:
- Pilot success criteria: 30% cost reduction on batch jobs (compare baseline Q4), p95 latency <= 300ms for chat after canary, and <5% error rate on production calls.
- Suggest we run a 2-week canary on 10% of chat traffic and parallel batch runs to measure cost delta. I’ll prepare an instrumentation checklist (traces, token-level cost, cache hit rates).
- For procurement: I can produce a one-page SOW + a technical appendix describing data handling, logging, and SOC2 scope to accelerate legal review.

Marissa — if you want, I’ll draft the SOW and send to Tom/Sabrina by Friday. Vivek, can you confirm resource availability for the canary (engineer hours + infra)?
